Winston Zeddemore sits beside him, bracing as they take a sharp turn, the city lights flashing past. The No Ghosts symbol on the side of the vehicle glints under the streetlamps as they race toward the call.

They hoist a new logo into place, identical to the original 'No Ghosts' design except the ghost inside the red circle holds up two fingers in a peace sign. Venkman arrives at the firehouse

description: A bright flash erupted from deep within the excavation site, followed instantly by a shout from Stantz. Venkman, Spengler, the police officers, and the supervisor all reacted at once, their attention snapping toward the hole as the light faded and the echo of the cry hung in the air.

Stantz shouts from deep in the hole
Bright flash occurs deep in the hole

name: Spengler Explains the Pneumatic Railway, Stantz Reports Depth
description: Venkman stood nearby, confused. Spengler began explaining that they were in the remains of the New York Pneumatic Railway, an experimental subway system from around 1870 that used fan-forced air to propel trains. At the same time, Stantz spoke over the walkie-talkie, noting that they had reached the deepest point possible under Manhattan without digging further. Spengler turned his attention to Stantz and asked for the current instrument reading.

Stantz reports depth limitations under Manhattan
Spengler asks Stantz for the current reading

name: Stantz Collects Slime Sample and Fends Off Attack
description: Hanging from a cable above a glowing, pulsating river of slime, Stantz detaches a device from his utility belt and fires a telescoping fishing pole with a scoop on the end. He lowers it into the slime, collects a sample, and begins retracting the pole. Suddenly, a grotesque arm with long skeletal fingers surges upward from the slime and grabs at his feet. He jerks his legs up just as several more arms burst out, flailing and grasping at the air beneath his boots. The slime churns violently. Stantz shouts into his radio, 'Haul me up, Venkman! Now!'

Grotesque arms emerge from slime and attack Stantz
Stantz calls for emergency extraction via radio

name: Stantz Discovers Van Horne Station
description: Stantz floats near the top of a chamber lined with smooth, rounded tiles, their surfaces covered in colorful Art Nouveau mosaics. His flashlight sweeps across the walls, glinting off the polished enamel. He holds a walkie-talkie close and speaks in a hushed tone. 'This is it, boys, the end of the line. Van Horne Station. The old New York Pneumatic. It's still here.'

description: Stantz lowers himself down the airshaft in complete darkness, the sound of his breath muffled by the narrow walls around him. He speaks into the radio, guiding his team above as he continues the descent. When his feet find no solid ground, he swings freely, realizing he has reached the end of the shaft and entered a tunnel. Ray responds that they can't give up now, reminding Winston the holidays are coming and it's their busiest time of year. They get into the car.

description: Venkman and Stantz come out of a building carrying small boxes of coffee, sandwiches, and Danish, then begin walking up the street. Venkman says he can smell it—they're onto something big—and expects they'll make headlines. Stantz stops him, warning that they could get into serious trouble if anyone finds out, reminding him the judge forbade them from ghostbusting. description: Spengler enters the room and suggests checking the street for anything unusual. Stantz is already present, monitoring the area, and notes that any activity has quieted down. He reports over the radio that the reading is off the scale and calls for the team to lower him to the floor. Venkman and Spengler begin feeding out the cable, slowly lowering him down. description: Ray Stantz turns the key in Ecto-1's ignition, but the engine doesn't start. He tries again, and this time the engine sputters to life before breaking into a harsh grinding noise, clunking violently. Twisted pieces of metal fall from the engine onto the pavement. A thick cloud of black, sooty exhaust bursts from the tailpipe as the car shudders and finally dies. Stantz leans forward and gently bangs his forehead against the steering wheel.

name: Stantz and Winston Reflect on a Faded Legacy
description: Stantz tries to start the car, but the engine won't turn over. Winston tells him to give it up, saying the Ghostbusters are finished and that people, especially the younger generation, have already forgotten who they are. Stantz calls the kids ungrateful, reminding Winston of everything they did for the city. Winston responds by recalling their last major job—the destruction caused by the hundred-foot-tall marshmallow man and the damage to an uptown high-rise. Stantz, still attempting to start the car, says it was worth it, comparing their sacrifices to making a hamburger. When he turns the key again, the engine sputters to life briefly before grinding violently, clunking, and spewing black exhaust as pieces of metal fall to the pavement. The car shudders and dies. Frustrated, Stantz gently bangs his head on the steering wheel.
related_events: Winston expresses disillusionment about Ghostbusters' legacy
Winston recalls destruction caused by the marshmallow man
Stantz criticizes younger generation as ungrateful

name: Dana Returns Home with Groceries and a Baby
description: Dana Barrett arrives home pushing a baby buggy and carrying two full bags of groceries, struggling to open her purse to find her keys. The building superintendent, Frank, sees her but initially does nothing. When she asks for help, he reluctantly takes the grocery bags from her, muttering that it's not his job. As Dana sets the brakes on the buggy, Frank leans over and makes faces at the baby, Oscar, commenting on how good-looking the child is. Dana thanks him and says she’ll get the hang of things eventually. While still fumbling with her purse, she asks Frank about the radiator in her bedroom, reminding him she’d requested the repair last week. Frank responds by asking if he hasn’t already fixed it. At that moment, the baby buggy begins to vibrate, as if shaken by an unseen hand.

In the chaos, Dana sprints into the crosswalk, reaches the baby, and pulls it tightly into her arms. She holds the child, breathing heavily, her face flushed with relief. Dana realizes supernatural presence has returned

description: A Con Ed Supervisor arrives with two police officers and approaches Venkman and Spengler, who are pulling up a cable. The Supervisor demands to know what they are doing. Venkman, wearing a Nynex hardhat, acts annoyed and claims they are fixing phone lines, blaming Spengler when the Supervisor points out the phone lines are at the curb. Over Venkman's walkie-talkie, Stantz's voice calls for help, shouting that something is alive and eating his boots. Venkman quickly turns off the device. One of the officers says they checked and confirms neither man is with Con Ed or the phone company. Venkman pauses, then asks, 'Gas leak?'

name: Ghostbusters Rise from the Wreckage After Courtroom Specter Surge
description: Smoke swirls through the shattered courtroom as broken benches and scattered papers litter the floor. He slowly lifts his head from behind the remains of his overturned bench, scanning the room in stunned silence. Louis wriggles out from under a splintered chair, coughing and dazed. Around him, reporters and spectators push themselves up, murmuring in disbelief, their voices rising in a wave of excitement. The Prosecutor lies on the ground, attended by the Bailiff and Court Clerk, who kneel beside her with concerned expressions. The Ghostbusters climb to their feet, brushing debris off their uniforms, their faces breaking into wide grins as camera flashes erupt around them. Venkman straightens his jacket and says, 'Case closed, boys. We're back in business.' The crowd roars, clapping and cheering as the team stands together in the ruined courtroom.

Spectators react with amazement to supernatural manifestation

name: Vigo Emerges from the Painting
description: Janosz works late, focused on the painting of Vigo. Unseen by him, the eyes of the painted figure begin to glow. He touches his brush to the canvas, and a surge of red, crackling energy erupts from the painting, traveling through the brush and into his body, forcing him to his knees. The figure of Vigo steps out of the canvas, turns toward Janosz, and makes a dramatic gesture. In a commanding voice, Vigo declares himself the scourge of Carpathia and the sorrow of Moldavia, demanding obedience. Janosz, in agony, responds, 'Command me, lord.' Vigo proclaims that what was will be again, and that the season of evil has arrived. He orders Janosz to find him a child so he may live once more. Red-hot energy bolts shoot from Vigo's eyes into Janosz's, causing him to scream and collapse to his knees.

name: Dana Confronts Janosz at the Door During the Blackout

She opens it only a crack, keeping the chain fastened, and finds Janosz standing in the hallway, lit by the dim red glow of an emergency light. His eyes seem unfocused, his manner unnerving. The supervisor examined it and said he had never seen anything like it in his years working underground. He added that they had inspected the tunnel the following day and found nothing, suggesting the substance must have been placed there by someone else. At the defense table, Stantz reacted defensively, insisting he had seen the slime in the tunnel and that there had been thousands of gallons of it. Spengler offered a quiet comment that the slime might have been receding due to a tidal source, but Louis, seated nearby, expressed doubt that anyone would believe such an explanation. name: Avoiding Police Scrutiny with a Utility Cover
description: Spengler, wearing a hardhat, jackhammers a hole in the middle of East 77th Street, surrounded by safety cones, reflectors, and bright work lights. A police car turns onto the street, slows as it approaches the site, and stops nearby. The noise of the jackhammer drowns out the sound of the engine, and Spengler doesn’t notice the two officers inside watching him. Eventually, he looks up, sees the car, and freezes. The first officer rolls down the window and calls out, 'How ya doing?' Spengler, visibly tense, replies, 'Fine! It's cutting fine now.' The officer asks why they’re cutting into the street. Before Spengler can answer, Venkman and Stantz arrive, both wearing Con Ed hardhats. The officer turns to them. Venkman responds with irritation, 'What the hell's it look like we're doing? We're bustin out asses over here 'cause some douchebag downtown ain't got nothin' better to do than make idiots like us work late on a Friday night, right?' Spengler raises a fist in agreement. The officers accept the explanation. The first cop says, 'Okay, boys, take it easy,' and the car drives away. Spengler exhales deeply, rubs his shoulders, and mutters, 'You were supposed to help me with this.' Venkman smirks, 'You need the exercise.'

name: Louis's Summation and the Judge's Condemnation
description: Louis rises to deliver his closing argument and asks to approach the bench. The judge grants permission, growing impatient when Louis requests a drink of water. Louis begins speaking to the court, addressing the judge and the room, expressing that it is unfair to label his clients as frauds. He recounts being stuck in an elevator during the blackout and mentions turning into a dog, saying the Ghostbusters helped him. He returns to his seat. Stantz and Spengler bow their heads. Venkman pats Louis on the back. Spengler tells him it was concise and to the point. The judge stares in disbelief and demands if that is all. The judge denounces the performance as the worst he has ever heard, threatens to have Louis cited for contempt and disbarred, then finds Venkman, Stantz, and Spengler guilty on all charges, imposing fines and an eighteen-month sentence at Ryker's Island. He adds a personal condemnation, calling them fakes and charlatans, and declares that if not for the law, he would have them burned at the stake. Their attorney, Louis Tully, nervously flips through a stack of legal textbooks, expressing doubt about his ability to handle the case, as he mostly practices tax and probate law. Stantz tries to reassure him, noting they were arrested at night, so his night school degree should suffice. In the spectators' gallery, Venkman talks to Dana near the railing. She says she feels responsible for his being on trial. He jokes that if he gets conjugal visits, she should come see him in prison. She kisses him quickly and leaves. Venkman lingers for a moment, then returns to the defense table. At the prosecution table, Jack Hardemeyer, the mayor’s aide, speaks to the prosecutor, urging her to secure a swift and severe conviction. He emphasizes that the mayor and future governor will remember her cooperation. As he leaves, he passes the defense table, smirking, and taunts Venkman about the long list of charges, predicting he’ll only see them again at a parole hearing.
